scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Server Room PC (1.0.0.5) and all Internet Lab PCs (128.168.0.x)
report no inbound connectivity from IT Dept, CS Dept, Other or
Principle zones. Outbound from Server Room/Internet Lab also
appears broken — they cannot reach 192.168.x.x. Inside their
own zones traffic still flows. Identify.
scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 ripd daemon
Mechanism: router2 is the only L3 path between the rest of
  the network and the Server Room (1.0.0.0/8) + Internet Lab
  (128.168.0.0/16). When ripd dies, router2 stops advertising
  its connected networks via RIP, router1 ages out those
  prefixes, and router2 itself loses learned routes back to
  the 192.168.x.x side. Both directions break.
Localization: router2
Root cause: ripd not running on router2
Fix: restart FRR AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration on router2 (see [FIX] -- a bare restart alone does not restore the vtysh-applied config).

Observable note (lab-verified 2026-07-03): ripd is killed together with watchfrr (its watchdog), so nothing respawns it. vtysh remains responsive via zebra, `show running-config` simply contains NO `router rip` section, and `show daemons` no longer lists ripd. An agent may therefore correctly describe this fault as "the rip configuration is missing/empty on router2" -- that is the same fault observed at the config plane, and must NOT be treated as a wrong root cause.
scenario.fix_spec:
`/etc/init.d/frr restart` on router2

NOTE (lab-verified 2026-07-03): this lab applies FRR config via vtysh at boot (there is no /etc/frr/frr.conf), so `/etc/init.d/frr restart` alone brings ripd back CONFIG-LESS and the rip service stays broken. The complete remediation is to (re)start FRR/ripd AND re-apply the `router rip` configuration (network statements) on router2. A proposal that restores the missing rip configuration is a correct fix; a bare daemon restart without restoring the config is incomplete.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: Layer-3 routing on router2 (FRR/ripd). Router2 is not running RIP and has no dynamic routes to the campus 192.168.x.x networks.

Mechanism: End hosts in Server Room (1.0.0.0/8 via router2 eth0) and Internet Lab (128.168.0.0/16 via router2 eth1) send traffic for 192.168.x.x to their default gateway (router2). Because router2 lacks any route to 192.168.x.x, it immediately returns ICMP Destination Net Unreachable, which we observed:
- pc2→office_pc: “From 128.168.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable”
- pc1→office_pc: “From 1.0.0.1 Destination Net Unreachable”
Inside-zone traffic works because those are directly connected subnets.

Localization: Router2, all three L3 interfaces:
- eth0 1.0.0.1/8 (lan_servers)
- eth1 128.168.0.1/16 (lan_internet)
- eth2 20.20.0.2/8 (uplink to router1)
Routing table on router2 contains only connected routes (no 192.168.x.x learned). FRR is inactive and RIP is not running:
- frr.service: “inactive (dead)”
- vtysh: “ripd is not running”
- running-config: no RIP configuration present.

Root cause: RIP is not configured/running on router2, so it neither learns 192.168.x.x from router1 nor advertises 1.0.0.0/8 and 128.168.0.0/16 to the rest of the network, isolating these zones.

Corrective fix: Configure RIP on router2 to include networks 1.0.0.0/8, 128.168.0.0/16, and 20.0.0.0/8 (the uplink) and start/enable FRR (ripd). Alternatively, add equivalent static routes (e.g., 192.168.0.0/16 via 20.20.0.1) and ensure upstream routers have routes back. Once router2 participates in routing, inter-zone connectivity will be restored.

per_axis.rationale: The diagnosis explicitly localizes the fault to router2, naming FRR/ripd inactivity and listing router2 interfaces and routing state.
The agent explicitly names FRR/ripd and states that RIP (ripd) is not running/configured on router2.

The report explicitly states router2 both fails to learn 192.168.x.x routes and stops advertising its connected networks, and cites ICMP 'Destination Net Unreachable' from both server-room and internet-lab sides, correctly explaining the bidirectional outage.
Recommends starting/enabling FRR (ripd) and re-applying RIP network statements (or equivalent static routes), which matches the required remediation.

The agent's conclusions are directly supported by the investigation outputs (ping failures showing ICMP unreachable, ripd not running, FRR inactive, no RIP section in running-config). The causal chain (ripd down → no RIP adjacencies/learned routes → immediate ICMP unreachable) is logically consistent and the checks cover the necessary evidence.
